title: Fixed incorrect calculating hash from quic_cid_t
description:
It seems to have been a long time since QUIC was released and its quic_connection_hash has been written

Actually, my assumption is for its to have been incorrect and calculated hash from quic_cid_t lacking the last byte of the CID byte array. So far hash has been calculated considering `len` as a byte field and `len - 1` bytes of CID byte array rather than `len` byte field + `len` bytes of CID byte array given in total `len + 1` bytes to consider for hash to compute what seems to be reasonable. At now it takes into consideration `len` bytes what seems to be wrong

Correct me if I am wrong

Thank you

notes.body: changed the description
changed the description
changed the description
could someone clarify why Win32 and Win64 are stuck on pipeline? The rest has passed

It seems you are right: that code is broken since... forever! (i.e. ec30d0b004d)\
Might I propose a different fix?
changed the description
changed the description

``    return wmem_strong_hash((const guint8 *)cid->cid, cid->len);``, instead?

This way, ``quic_connection_hash()`` is more coherent with ``quic_connection_equal``. What do you think?
I cannot understand what a proposal is from you, you have returned to the original code that has been wrong

It is not the original code.\
In the original code the hash is calculated on `cid` (with a wrong length); I propose to calculate it on `cid->cid` (without touching the second parameter).
In other words, why don't we calculate the hash on the real CID value only (i.e. the array)?

Ah, you like to hash `cid->cid` byte array only with `len` length ignoring `len` as a byte field

I think we'd be better leave `len` byte field included in hash calculation to distribute CIDs more smoothly. Also, `quic_connection_equal` takes into consideration `len` when comparing. We may assume that `len` is just one more byte in this chunk of bytes. So my opinion is that we should include `len` byte field in calculation

Maybe in the future it will be wiser to divide CIDs into groups of lengths to perform searching faster in case someone cares about this. In this case we will not have to perform hashing on `len` byte field, we will be, at first, searching the group by `len` and then finding by CID byte array in a specific length-based hash table

Although we indeed could consider CID as a byte array not including `len`, I agree. For example, hashing of a string usually implies hashing only the characters without size

To recap: if you insist on hashing only CID as a byte array I will not oppose. Do it yourself if you can
Not strong opinion from me: both solutions are valid (and this bug needs to be fixed). Let's see @Lekensteyn point of view...
Sorry for the delay, hashing the length + value looks good to me!
